core_obligations: Construct the functor v (proof lines 9735-9748): for an object V -> p(U) of D/p(U), fibredness provides the strongly cartesian morphism V x_{p(U)} U -> U, and the resulting functor v : D/p(U) -> C/U, V/p(U) |-> V x_{p(U)} U/U, is continuous by definition of the topology on C and is a right adjoint of p by the definition of strongly cartesian morphisms.
Identify the pushforward (proof lines 9749-9755): in the continuous-adjoint situation of the sites chapter, the sheaf pi_{U,*}F is V |-> F(V x_{p(U)} U).

Get the section and the identities (proof lines 9757-9764): the same functor v is also cocontinuous because all morphisms in coverings of C are strongly cartesian, so it defines a morphism of topoi sigma with sigma^{-1} = pi_{U,*}; since pi_U^{-1}G is U'/U |-> G(p(U')/p(U)), one gets sigma^{-1} pi_U^{-1} = id, hence pi_U o sigma = id.
proof_roadmap: Use fibredness to build v : D/p(U) -> C/U and note it is continuous with right adjoint p.
Identify pi_{U,*} with the pullback along v, and note v is also cocontinuous because covering morphisms are strongly cartesian.
Conclude that v induces the required section sigma, with sigma^{-1} = pi_{U,*} and pi_U sigma = id.
difficulty_reason: The lemma provides a section sigma of the localised morphism of topoi pi_U whose pullback is the pushforward of pi_U (statement lines 9719-9732). The proof (proof lines 9734-9764) builds the functor V |-> V x_{p(U)} U from fibredness, observes it is continuous with right adjoint p, identifies pi_{U,*} with pullback along it, and then uses cocontinuity — covering morphisms of C being strongly cartesian — to obtain sigma and the two identities. H2: one explicit construction plus two identity checks, written out.
